retrieved_evidence.text: Alder Relay 2.4 normative retry policy, approved 2028-02-04. The default total_attempts value is 1, including the initial attempt. A signed deployment configuration may override total_attempts to an integer from 1 to 4. Only a transport timeout is retryable; HTTP 4xx responses remain final and must not be retried. The deployment value takes precedence over this default. A retry allowance is a ceiling, not evidence that any request actually retried.

Signed fleet configuration register, captured 2028-02-12. Cedar production runs Alder Relay 2.4 with effective total_attempts=2. Juniper production remains on Alder Relay 1.8 with effective total_attempts=3. These are the complete current values for the two named clusters. This register records configured limits, not per-request execution history.

Alder Relay 1.8 operator quickstart. Scope: release 1.8 only. A request may be attempted at most three times in total: the initial attempt and at most two retries. Only a transport timeout is retryable. HTTP 4xx responses are final and must not be retried. This document is not a policy for later major policy revisions.

Training slide 17 was labelled 'Alder Relay 2.4: three attempts everywhere'. Editorial correction dated 2028-02-10: the slide copied the old 1.8 quickstart and was never approved as the 2.4 retry policy. Do not use it to determine 2.4 defaults or a cluster's effective value. Use the approved 2.4 normative policy together with the signed fleet configuration register.

retrieved_evidence.text: KiteLoad 5.2 current configuration capture dated 2028-05-21: automatic_retry=true; max_retries=2; retryable_condition=transport_timeout. max_retries excludes the initial attempt, so the current ceiling is three total attempts. HTTP 429 is not retryable under this configuration. This capture is not a historical configuration snapshot for any earlier run.

Retained completion receipt for KiteLoad run R-731, dated 2028-04-03: final_status=SUCCEEDED; output_rows=240. The receipt does not record attempt_count, retry_count, per-attempt timestamps, HTTP status codes, exception classes, or the configuration revision used by the run. A successful final status alone does not distinguish first-attempt success from success after a retry.

Archived alert card transcription for R-731: 'Badge: 3; delivery complete'. The export contains no badge legend and no per-attempt events. It does not say that the badge is an attempt or retry count. No upstream response code or rate-limit event was included.

Historical evidence inventory for R-731, compiled 2028-05-22. The only retained run-specific artifacts supplied here are the completion receipt and alert-card transcription. The worker attempt ledger was not exported before its 24-hour retention expired. No run-time configuration snapshot, upstream request trace, or per-attempt failure record is available in this evidence bundle. Establishing that a retry happened requires an authoritative retry counter or linked per-attempt execution records. Attributing an attempt failure to upstream rate limiting requires a corresponding upstream response or correlated failure record; retry settings alone cannot establish a cause.
